newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK DEPOS, BONDS STEADY, ECU/DRS AROUND 308.65.
newsitem.headline: GREEK DEPOS, BONDS STEADY, ECU/DRS AROUND 308.65.

text.p: Greek depos were holding Thursday
levels around mid-session but forex forwards were trading
slightly higher in periods from three- to six-months, dealers
said. Greek markets were closed on Assumption Day on Friday.
The drachma was hovering below 309 around, trading currently
around 308.65 after opening at 308.40/50 and bonds were little
changed, traders said.
"Depos are stable, having adjusted for the central bank's 30
basis point cut in its basic depo facility rate today," said a
money market dealer. "The market is very quiet."
The Bank of Greece slashed its basic depo facility rate 30
basis points to 11.30 percent effective today but left its floor
rate unchanged at 9.60 percent.
Implied drachma rates from forex forwards were holding but
for a slight increase in periods from three-to-six months,
dealers said.
"Liquidity is tight and the money market looks to forex for
rate clues," said a senior dealer at a private bank.
Fixed coupon bonds which received a boost from the central
bank's basic depo facility rate cut that lowered the cost of
carry were marking time, awaiting to hear the amount of
seven-year FRNs that the ministry will auction on August 21.
Greece is to auction seven-year floaters on August 21 but
the treasury has yet to announce the amount.
"Prices of fixed coupon bonds are holding in quiet
dealings," said a bond trader at a foreign bank. "The question
mark is how much money the ministry will seek to raise through
its FRN auction."
The dealer added that the central bank's rate cut helped
coupon bonds catch their breath but noted that the big problem
with coupon bonds continued to be the lack of a sufficiently
large end-user pool of investors.
The 10-year bond was trading below 95, around 94.65/95,
dealers said.
The market was quoted at 157.20/30 from Thursday's 157.150
fix, the dollar at 284.77/87 from 288.970 and the ecu at
"Ecu/drachma is trading around 308.65/70 after opening at
308.40/50," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "There was
some buying for ecus earlier on but ecu selling emerged around
308.75/80 that sent ecu/drachma lower."
Forex dealers said the central bank's move to sell
ecu/drachma last Thursday gave the market a hint that the
central bank wanted the drachma to strengthen against the ecu.
The Bank of Greece sold about 30 million ecus for drachmas
at Thursday's fixing, pushing ecu/drachma down to 308.60, about
40 to 50 basis points below market levels.
"The big story is dollar/mark and Buba's next move," said a
senior dealer. "A rise in mark rates will hurt Greek assets
markets and weaken the drachma."
Some mark/drachma buying drove the mark up against the
drachma at 157.15/20.
The National Bank of Greece quoted the following mid-session
rates:

** One week at 11.10-11.60
